# Derivatives, Partial Derivatives, and Directional Derivatives

Calculus underpins every gradient-based learning algorithm. This note builds the mathematical foundation from the single-variable derivative through partial derivatives, the gradient, and directional derivatives.

## Single-Variable Derivatives: The Formal Limit Definition

f'(x) = lim_{h→0} [f(x+h) − f(x)] / h. For f(x) = x², f'(x) = 2x. Rules: linearity, product, quotient, chain rule.

## Partial Derivatives: Fixing All But One Variable

∂f/∂xᵢ = lim_{h→0} [f(x + h·eᵢ) − f(x)] / h. For f(x,y) = x²y + y³: ∂f/∂x = 2xy, ∂f/∂y = x² + 3y².

```python
def partial_deriv(f, x, i, h=1e-5):
    xf, xb = x.copy(), x.copy()
    xf[i] += h; xb[i] -= h
    return (f(xf) - f(xb)) / (2 * h)
```

## The Gradient Vector

∇f(x) = [∂f/∂x₁, …, ∂f/∂xₙ]ᵀ ∈ ℝⁿ. Points in the direction of steepest ascent. Gradient descent: θ ← θ − η∇L(θ).

## Directional Derivatives

D_{v̂}f(x) = ∇f(x)·v̂ where v̂ is a unit vector. Reduces to ∂f/∂xᵢ when v̂ = eᵢ.

## Why the Gradient Maximises the Directional Derivative

By Cauchy-Schwarz: ∇f·v̂ ≤ ‖∇f‖·‖v̂‖ = ‖∇f‖. Equality when v̂ ∥ ∇f. Maximum directional derivative = ‖∇f‖; steepest descent is −∇f.

## Total Derivative vs. Partial Derivative

Total derivative Df(x)[v] = ∇f(x)·v is the best linear approximation: f(x+v) ≈ f(x) + ∇f(x)·v. Total derivative of composition: df/dt = (∂f/∂x)(dx/dt) + (∂f/∂y)(dy/dt).

## Implicit Differentiation

For F(x, y) = 0: dy/dx = −(∂F/∂x)/(∂F/∂y). In meta-learning: dφ*/dθ = −[∇²_{φφ}L_in]⁻¹ · ∇²_{φθ}L_in via the implicit function theorem.

## Higher-Order Partials and Clairaut's Theorem

Mixed partials ∂²f/∂xᵢ∂xⱼ commute when continuous (Clairaut's theorem) → Hessian Hᵢⱼ is symmetric. Symmetry gives real eigenvalues — the principal curvatures of the loss landscape.

> **Key insight:** The condition number κ = λ_max/λ_min of the Hessian determines how many gradient descent steps are needed. Adam's adaptive rates reduce the effective condition number.
